title: Dependency outage: one container goes silent while its peers carry on

problem.summary: A dependency is stopped, so the container serving it stops producing kernel events almost entirely. No new container appears - this fault REMOVES a workload rather than adding one - so any rule that looks for a newcomer cannot find it. The portable signature is silence: exactly one container that was busy falls to about 1% of its own baseline rate while every other container keeps running.
symptoms: requests through one path fail or hang rather than slowing
one container stops producing kernel events while its peers do not
no new container appeared during the window

discriminators.signal: each container's total kernel event rate, incident window against its own baseline, ranked lowest first
discriminators.this_problem: exactly ONE container falls to 0.09-1.19% of its baseline rate while the next quietest container is still at 23-89%. That container is the stopped dependency and it is the answer to WHERE
discriminators.not_this_problem: nothing falls that far, or several containers fall together - several falling together is host-wide, not one dependency
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED on 6 runs across two applications, 28-09-2026. The silent container ran at 1360, 1382 and 1521 events/s before against 1, 2 and 5 during on one application; 377, 462 and 422 against 4, 3 and 4 on the other. Exactly one such container in all 6 runs, ranked first by this measure in all 6.

discriminators.signal: getrusage rate in the container that CALLS the stopped dependency
discriminators.this_problem: on one of the two applications the caller storms: 6.7/s before against 2474-2701/s during, a 371-404x rise, while sibling containers running the same image stay flat
discriminators.not_this_problem: on the OTHER application the same fault produced NO getrusage rise at all - 1.0x, measured on 2 runs. Absence of a storm is therefore not evidence against this problem, and this signal must never be required. Use it to corroborate and to name the victim, never to decide
discriminators.evidence: MEASURED 28-09-2026 on both applications. Portable on only one of them, which is why the silence test above is the deciding one.

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: the stopped dependency can be named directly from the kernel trace
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: a stopped container simply stops producing events. Absence is not distinguishable from a container that was always idle without knowing the topology, and a kernel trace carries no service names.
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: name the SPINNING container and say its dependency is unreachable. Identifying which dependency needs spans, logs or a topology map.

unverified_do_not_claim.claim: getrusage is the mechanism rather than an artefact of this runtime
unverified_do_not_claim.measurement: measured on two Sock Shop runs, both Java callers. Whether a Go or Node caller produces the same storm was not tested.
unverified_do_not_claim.consequence: treat the SHAPE - one container's syscall rate exploding while identical siblings stay flat - as the discriminator, and the specific syscall as a Java detail.

reproduction.teardown: the recipe restores state; verify against /sys/fs/cgroup
harness_only: the fault is injected as a sidecar container, which is a property of our harness. In production the same mechanism occurs inside an existing service - so the SHAPE transfers, the newcomer shortcut does not

collection_order.why_these: MEASURED BASIS. Every discriminator in this blueprint is a share of these event groups within one container. Nothing else in the trace is required, and no other modality is used - this blueprint was built and validated on kernel traces alone.

processing.expect: a CTF directory with metadata and channel streams

processing.step: Find containers that are active during the window and absent before it
processing.expect: one container with substantial traffic during the window and none before. If none appears, this blueprint does not apply - say so and stop

processing.step: Measure what share of its own events that container spends on each kind of work
processing.expect: the share profile below, within the measured range

processing.step: rank every container by its incident event rate divided by its own baseline rate, lowest first, and name the one that went silent
processing.expect: containers ranked by how far their own rate fell, the lowest named by pid_ns, and the next-lowest reported so the size of the gap is visible

processing.step: Apply the rules and emit the verdict
processing.expect: name the SILENT container by its pid_ns, its before and after rates, and the next-quietest container's rate as the contrast
one page showing the shares, the cut, and what was ruled out

outputs.contains: culprit container pid_ns, its event shares, and the shares of every other container for comparison
per-container event shares for the window
each family's measured share on the deciding axis, with this run's value marked

verdict_when: exactly one container that was busy before falls to {SILENT_MAX_SHARE} or less of its own baseline event rate
the next quietest container is still at {SILENT_PEER_MIN_SHARE} or more of its own baseline, so the drop is an outlier rather than a general slowdown
no new container appeared - this fault removes a workload rather than adding one

rule_out.when: a container IS new to the window - this fault removes a container, it does not add one
many containers fell together rather than one falling alone. Measured, the next quietest container here still runs at 23-89% of its baseline
the suspect is still running but held at a flat ceiling. A stopped dependency goes to near zero, not to a steady reduced rate

decision.root_cause_is: the container that went silent. It is the stopped dependency and it is the answer to WHERE. A container that storms on getrusage is the VICTIM calling into it, and naming that one is the mistake this blueprint exists to prevent

provenance.authored_by: measured from StrataTrace v2 kernel traces
provenance.notes: Rewritten 28-09-2026 after testing the generated version against the traces. Its verdict_when said 'a container is new to the window' while its own applicability said 'no new container appeared' - a generator template had overwritten a correct summary. The trace agrees with the summary: no newcomer in 3 of 3 runs on one application. The deciding test is now silence, measured on both applications, and the getrusage storm is kept as corroboration with its single-application scope stated.

apply_when: requests through one path fail or hang rather than slowing
one container stopped producing kernel events while its peers did not
no new container appeared during the window
do_not_apply_when: a new container appeared - use the newcomer blueprints instead
every container moved together, which is host-wide
the suspect is running at a reduced but steady rate rather than near zero
applicability.cheap_precheck: rank containers by incident event rate divided by their own baseline rate. If the lowest is at or below {SILENT_MAX_SHARE} and the next is at or above {SILENT_PEER_MIN_SHARE}, this is it.

capabilities_required.why: WHERE: the stopped dependency IS the silent container, so this discriminator names the target directly. Measured to rank it first in 6 of 6 runs across both applications.

stopping_conditions.conclude: exactly one container fell to {SILENT_MAX_SHARE} or less of its own baseline while the next quietest stayed at {SILENT_PEER_MIN_SHARE} or more
stopping_conditions.stop_and_switch: several containers fell together, which is host-wide; or the lowest is only moderately reduced, which is throttling rather than an outage
stopping_conditions.stop_insufficient: no container fell far below its own baseline. Say so rather than naming the busiest container, which is the victim at best

applicable_symptoms: requests through one path fail or hang rather than slowing
one service's resource use rises sharply while its peers do not
a dependency produces little or no traffic

historical_effectiveness.note: shares measured on 5 runs of this family

evidence_sufficiency.if_below_floor: report the per-container before and after rates and say that no container went silent
evidence_sufficiency.report_when_stuck: the ranked list of containers by incident rate over baseline rate, with the pid_ns of the lowest
